result:
Kept the count but rephrased it; did not adopt the identifier suggestion.

What changed: the cycle phrase now reads "in the cycle with only two open issues left" (request and condition c4) — end-of-cycle triage language a lead would actually use, instead of the test-like "with exactly two open issues". The query, seed, and decoys are untouched ("only two left" is still exactly two).

What I kept and why: the count itself must stay and must do identifying work — the brief mandates testing `D:issue_count`, and a scenario can only test it if the solver has to check it. Citing the issue identifier (ATLAS-1) would pin the target uniquely, so the count would be redundant and no decoy could compete; a careful colleague would agree the identifier defeats the test. The project is already named (Harbor Launch), so the count is now the single load-bearing discriminator, phrased as naturally as the fact allows.
